title: An optimized workflow to measure bacterial predation in microplates
protocol: Turn on the plate reader.
Prepare the protocol on the plate reader controlling software.
Set pre-set temperature to 25°C.
Set continuous shaking with double orbital shaking, frequency 282 cpm for 15 minutes.
Set SYBR Green fluorescence read at 490 nm excitation and 520 nm emission.
Set gain with the Standard DNA curve.
Read absorbance at 600 nm (OD 600).
Transfer 198 μL from each cleared culture into three different wells of a black 96-well plate with transparent flat bottom.
Add 2 μL of SYBR Green to each well, protected from light.
Load the plate without lid inside the plate reader.

Calculate the average SYBR Green fluorescence value due to Bdellovibrio bacteriovorus by subtracting the average SYBR Green fluorescence value due to E. coli from the total SYBR Green fluorescence value for each culture.
Extrapolate the number of B. bacteriovorus cells using the predator standard curve.
Exclude outlier wells if their standard deviation represents more than 15% of the mean SYBR Green fluorescence value.
Set the plate reader protocol for the killing assay at a temperature of 30°C.
Enable continuous shaking with double orbital shaking at a frequency of 282 cpm.
Read absorbance at 600 nm (OD600).
Configure mCherry fluorescence read settings: excitation at 587 nm, emission at 610 nm, gain set to 70.
Optimize the gain setting for mCherry fluorescence based on your plate reader setup.
Set intervals between acquisitions to 20 minutes.
Prepare a black 96-well plate with a transparent flat bottom.
Add DNB supplemented with 2 mM CaCl2 and 3 mM MgCl2 to the wells.
Add prey suspension to achieve a final OD600 of 1.
Add B. bacteriovorus predator at a concentration of 5-10 × 107 cells/mL.
Ensure the final volume in each well is 300 μL.
Adjust the volume of B. bacteriovorus inoculum according to results from the SYBR Green assay for consistency across strains.
Use repetitive pipettes for accurate liquid transfer and reproducibility over technical and biological replicates.
Subculture antibiotics-resistant B. bacteriovorus in medium without antibiotics before the killing assay.
Use a wild-type E. coli strain as prey for both subculture and assay when using B. bacteriovorus strains with replicative plasmids.
Monitor predation-independent lysis by adding prey alone in DNB supplemented with salts to control wells.
Add Bdellovibrio predator alone to monitor the fluorescence signal in absence of prey.
Maintain the same density of predator or prey cells as used in the predatory mix in a 300 μL final volume for controls.
Load the 96-well plate without lid into the plate reader.
Start the killing kinetics for 18 hours using specified settings.
Format the input file according to the provided template.
Launch Rstudio.
Execute CuRveR by running "CuRveR::run_curver()" in the R console.
Plot your data using an appropriate method.
